messages:
oliver: Heads-up — hitting ReferenceError: require is not defined when importing @redwood/inference from a Next.js app-router server component deployed to Vercel Edge. Works fine on Node server runtime.

maya: Oof. That usually means Next picked a CJS entrypoint. Which import path are you using?

oliver: import Inference from '@redwood/inference' in a server component (server/page.tsx). Build stack during prerender: 
```
ReferenceError: require is not defined
    at Object.<anonymous> (/var/task/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs.js:1:20)
```

tom: Are you on appDir + experimental edge runtime? Edge disallows require. The SDK should expose a proper ESM/edge entrypoint or exports map.

eva: Can you paste package.json inside node_modules/@redwood/inference? Usually main/module/exports determine what Next bundles.

oliver: Sure — trimmed: 
```
{
  "name": "@redwood/inference",
  "version": "0.7.2",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```
No "exports" field.

maya: Ah — without exports, Next/webpack sometimes falls back to main (CJS). Quick workaround: import explicitly from the ESM build: `import Inference from '@redwood/inference/dist/index.esm.js'` or use dynamic import in the server component: `const { default: Inference } = await import('@redwood/inference')` so bundler picks the ESM.

tom: Note: dynamic import helps, but we saw cases where Next still bundles the CJS shim for edge. Another workaround is a webpack alias in next.config.js: 
```
module.exports = {
  webpack: (config) => {
    config.resolve.alias['@redwood/inference'] = path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.esm.js')
    return config
  }
}
```

eva: That works as a short-term hack but is nasty. For DX, we should publish an "edge" or "browser" entry in package.json and an exports map so bundlers choose the right target automatically. Also ensure the types field remains valid for TS consumers.

oliver: Also ran into TypeScript errors when using `import type` vs runtime import — types came from `dist/index.d.ts` but runtime was CJS, so mismatches.

maya: Can you open a minimal repro? If we have a small app router repo that reproduces the error on Vercel Edge we can attach to an issue.

oliver: I'll push repro. Immediate plan: try webpack alias, then dynamic import fallback. I'll paste working snippet if successful.

devex-bot: Created issue #1423 — "JS SDK: app-router + edge runtime ESM/CJS mismatch and typings" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/1423

tom: Long-term: publish an explicit exports map, add an `edge` entrypoint (pure ESM, no require), and run a Next+Vercel edge smoke test in CI. Also add a docs note about using the ESM build in RSC/edge.

eva: Also add a small helper function in the SDK repo `src/edge-adapter.ts` that re-exports only edge-safe code and keeps any native bindings out. That should reduce the need for consumers to hack webpack.

oliver: Thanks all — will comment on #1423 with repro and logs. If anyone wants to try the alias trick now ping me.

maya: FYI also ran into this once where `typesVersions` in package.json helped TS pick the right types for ESM consumers. Might be worth adding to the package.

oliver: attaching build snippet from Vercel logs: "Error: ReferenceError: require is not defined" during lambda build step — exact line points at dist/index.cjs.js.

maya: Good repro. Filing PR checklist: exports map + edge entry + CI smoke, and update README with Next app-router guidance.

oliver: I'll assign myself to the repro + comment on the issue. Thanks!
